main_text.l: NEc Musa possēt dicere: beatè Vena fluxit. Quid ergo? Rorat carmina in Corde, non in venis. Deabus ille VVTSSIUS vel Phœbus est, vel fallit. Probatur forma Corporis, et Mentis, his Deabus. Sed prodit his Amoribus, quod nos latere nolunt. Itáne, FLOS amabilis, DEAS amare nôsti? Id jure juro: Vatibus hic ardor est canendus. Canemus: Vivat VVTSSIUS, et turba dicat: AMEN.

page.notes: The large N of the first line is joined to "Ec" as printed. The first verse line reads "possët" with the diaeresis as printed; I have written "possēt" in the transcription and the scan is faint there. "VVTSSIUS" is printed as shown. The final word is printed with a decorated A and a flourish, transcribed as AMEN.
